about.title: Antioch Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription:
Antioch sits at the east end of Contra Costa County, and a lot of daily life here runs along SR-4, Lone Tree Way and Hillcrest Avenue. Those three corridors also show up most often in the city's public collision records. In 2025, the most recent final reporting year, Antioch logged 293 injury collisions. Those crashes left 386 people injured and took 9 lives. The records also show reports clustering on Sundays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m.

If one of those crashes was yours, you are probably sorting out car repairs, medical appointments and calls from an adjuster all at once. LawProactive exists to take one item off that list. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims in Antioch and the surrounding county. That attorney works on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case produces a recovery. You talk with them and decide whether it is a fit.

whyChoose.title: Why Antioch Drivers Reach Out Through LawProactive

items.title: The clock matters, and it is shorter than many expect
items.desc: California gives you two years to file most car accident injury claims, but if a city, county or state agency is involved, a formal claim may be due in as little as six months. Connecting early gives an attorney room to sort out who the responsible parties are.

items.title: Being partly at fault does not end your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery is reduced by your share of blame rather than erased. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to pin more of the crash on you than the facts support.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Every attorney in the LawProactive network handles car accident cases on contingency, and California places no cap on compensation for pain, suffering and other non-economic losses. Your connection through us costs nothing.

items.question: My crash happened on SR-4 in Antioch. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It can. SR-4 is a state highway, and if road conditions, signage or a public agency's vehicle played a role, part of your claim may involve a government entity. Claims against public entities in California often must be filed within six months, far sooner than the usual two-year deadline, so it is worth getting an attorney's read on this quickly.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are generally not obligated to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is usually wise to hold off until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions in ways that can shrink your claim. You can politely decline and let your attorney handle communication instead.

items.question: What should I save from the scene of an Antioch collision?
items.answer: Keep everything: photos of the vehicles and intersection, the Antioch Police report number, names of any witnesses, and all medical records and bills. Do not repair or dispose of your car until photos are taken and, ideally, an attorney has reviewed the damage. Small details like a dashcam clip or a receipt for a rental car often end up mattering later.
